evals.expected_output: Refactored component with: typed Product interface, discriminated union for loading/error/success states, proper error handling for the fetch, accessible markup, extracted data fetching concern, no `any`
expectations: Product type/interface with specific fields (id, name, price with correct types), not `any`
Component state models all three states: loading, error, success — using discriminated union or separate state variables
Error state is rendered with a user-facing message and ideally a retry mechanism
Loading state is rendered (spinner, skeleton, or loading text)
Data fetching is not a bare fetch-in-useEffect — either extracted to a custom hook, uses a library pattern, or at minimum handles cleanup/AbortController
No use of `any` anywhere
Semantic HTML is used — list elements use ul/li or similar, not bare divs
Empty state is handled (what if the array is empty?)

evals.prompt: build me a reusable modal dialog component in typescript react. it should be accessible (keyboard nav, focus trap, screen reader announcements), support custom content, and handle escape to close. i dont want it to use any specific UI library, just plain react + typescript.
evals.expected_output: Accessible modal with: typed props, portal rendering, focus trap, escape key handling, aria attributes, scroll lock, proper ref forwarding, controlled open/close
expectations: Renders via React portal (createPortal) to avoid z-index/overflow issues
Implements focus trap — focus stays within modal when tabbing, returns to trigger element on close
Sets appropriate ARIA attributes: role=dialog, aria-modal=true, aria-labelledby or aria-label
Handles Escape key to close the modal
Locks body scroll when modal is open
Props are properly typed with an interface — children, isOpen, onClose at minimum
No use of `any` type
Clicking the backdrop/overlay closes the modal
Supports ref forwarding or exposes a way to imperatively control focus

evals.expected_output: Optimized form with: typed field names (no bare string), isolated re-renders per field, proper form validation types, accessible labels, memoization where appropriate, typed onSubmit payload
expectations: Field names are typed — handleChange uses keyof FormData or a mapped type, not bare `string`
Re-renders are isolated so typing in one field doesn't re-render all 15 — via React.memo on child components, useRef for values, or uncontrolled inputs with refs
onSubmit parameter is properly typed (not `any`) with a specific form data interface
Form fields have associated labels (htmlFor + id or aria-label) for accessibility
No use of `any` type anywhere in the output
Validation is addressed — at minimum type-level (required fields, email format) or runtime validation
Submit handler prevents double submission or has some guard
The solution does not introduce external form libraries (user said no external libs)
